problem: Use pretrained video generators as transferable policy representations instead of assuming generic VLM features or direct visual imitation capture action-relevant dynamics.
contribution: Video Policy couples an SVD video U-Net to a diffusion action U-Net via intermediate denoising features. A two-stage video adaptation followed by an action head with stopped action gradients gives better results than joint end-to-end optimization. Video-only knowledge can transfer to tasks lacking action supervision, but those tasks still appear during video training.
algorithm: Condition SVD on current VAE image latent and CLIP instruction. At each denoising iteration, a CNN adapter combines five hidden video features (layers9,14,17,20,23) into the1Daction-UNet conditioning vector. Train video denoising, freeze the video network and train action diffusion; compare with joint and unadapted-video ablations. Generation and action denoising remain coupled at inference.
observations: Three RGB views: wrist and two scene cameras, concatenated into a25frame SVD-compatible sequence. RoboCasa predicts8frames/view plus padding; LIBERO uses two views with12frames/view. The real data also recordsT265pose, ArUcojaw aperture and load-cell force.
actions: Simulation uses7D gripper Cartesian pose/opening. Real policy predicts relative gripper pose, relative jaw position and absolute grasp force over32steps; robot executes24at30Hz with impedance control. A force-based extra closing correction is applied when predicted force exceeds actual measured force by300grams; this is part of the executed system, not an unassisted video-only policy.
embodiment_and_data: 24RoboCasa and10LIBERO tasks. Main RoboCasa model uses50human demonstrations/task, with a separate300MimicGen variant. Real tests have5tasks and200handheld-gripper demonstrations/task using the same effector as robot execution. Only one physical embodiment is evaluated; no actual SO101/ROSMASTER transfer.
experiments: RoboCasa50rollouts/task across5scenes; real table10rollouts/task for each of3generalization conditions. Study action/video objectives, prediction horizon and action supervision for half of tasks. Appendix clarifies the horizon study uses a different MimicGen-layout protocol from the standard all-OOD RoboCasa evaluation, so its curves should not be merged with the main table.
baselines: 3DA,DP3,ResNet/CLIP diffusion policy,GR00T,FPV,DP-VLA,UVA and LIBERO baselines. Some external baselines use300 or3000MimicGen demonstrations versus50human episodes for the main model. UVA and DP are adapted to three views; other results are taken from prior work. Comparison scope and data budgets therefore differ.

limitations: Video diffusion is explicitly a deployment bottleneck. Transparent objects, small-object localization under background shift and physically unrealistic future videos cause failures. Reported successes partly rely on impedance/force-corrected execution and a load cell unavailable on the current SO101/ROSMASTER grippers. A video predictor's good frames do not certify actual grasp forces or outcomes.
code_and_license: Seed repository https://github.com/cvlab-columbia/videopolicy and paper resource references were not inspected for code, SVD weights, demonstration or dataset licenses. Those terms are NOT_AUDITED separately; no code executed.
hardware_adaptation: ADAPT the training-time auxiliary-video/gradient-isolation ablation as an offline experiment, not the full SVD runtime. Nine-second A100 generation and eightA100 training make direct NX deployment implausible without substantial measured distillation. Current robots do not expose the paper's load-cell/impedance interface, so do not manufacture force labels or reproduce its closing correction by guessing servo positions.
